setting.time_period: Victorian England, 1860s, on a hot summer afternoon in May
setting.world: Realistic England giving way to Wonderland, an underground nonsensical fantasy dream-world beneath England
setting.description: A drowsy English riverbank and farm countryside framing a fall down a deep furnished well into an underground fantasy realm of long halls, small doors, lovely gardens, woods, a Duchess's smoky kitchen, a tea-table under trees, a ridged croquet-ground, seashore, and courtroom, all populated by talking animals, living playing cards, and magic food that changes size.

characters.name: Alice
characters.physical_description: A small young girl with long fair hair falling over her shoulders and bright eager eyes. She wears a simple Victorian child's dress with stockings and shoes, typical of a middle-class English schoolgirl.

characters.name: White Rabbit
characters.physical_description: A small white rabbit with pink eyes, ears and whiskers, standing upright. He wears a waistcoat with a waistcoat-pocket and watch.

characters.name: Dinah
characters.physical_description: A domestic tabby cat with soft fur. She is a dear quiet thing often seen purring by the fire, licking her paws and washing her face.

characters.name: Mouse
characters.physical_description: A small brown mouse with little bright eyes and a long tail. He is dripping wet from swimming, with fur clinging close and trembling to the end of his tail.

characters.name: Dodo
characters.physical_description: A large solemn dodo bird with shaggy grey-brown plumage, a big beak, and stubby wings. He stands upright and gestures with one finger pressed to his forehead.

characters.name: Lory
characters.physical_description: A small colorful parrot-like bird with draggled feathers from being wet. She has a sulky expression and bright plumage typical of a lory.

characters.name: Duck
characters.physical_description: A medium-sized duck with wet draggled feathers and a bill. He swims in the pool and sits in a ring on the bank with the other birds.

characters.name: Eaglet
characters.physical_description: A small young eagle with brown downy feathers and a hooked beak. He is small among the party of birds on the bank.

characters.name: Duchess
characters.physical_description: A broad-faced ugly woman with a heavy chin and sharp features. She wears a noble dress and sits on a three-legged stool nursing a baby.

characters.name: Caterpillar
characters.physical_description: A large blue caterpillar exactly three inches high with folded arms. He sits on top of a mushroom quietly smoking a long hookah.

characters.name: Pigeon
characters.physical_description: A large pigeon with grey feathers and beating wings. She sits in a nest in the highest tree in the wood guarding her eggs.

characters.name: Fish-Footman
characters.physical_description: A footman in livery with a fish-like face, powdered hair curled all over his head. He carries a great letter nearly as large as himself under his arm.

characters.name: Frog-Footman
characters.physical_description: A footman in livery with a round frog-like face and large eyes set very nearly at the top of his head. He has powdered curled hair and stares stupidly up into the sky.

characters.name: Cook
characters.physical_description: A stout woman cook in a kitchen dress with an apron. She carries a pepper-box and stands over a large cauldron stirring soup.

characters.name: Baby
characters.physical_description: A queer-shaped little baby with a very turn-up nose like a snout and extremely small eyes. It has arms and legs spread in all directions like a star-fish.

characters.name: Cheshire Cat
characters.physical_description: A large cat sitting on the hearth and on tree boughs, with very long claws and a great many teeth. He has a wide grin spreading from ear to ear that lingers after the rest of him vanishes.

characters.name: Hatter
characters.physical_description: A man with great curiosity in his eyes wearing a large hat. He sits at a tea-table with a teacup, bread-and-butter, and a pocket watch that tells the day of the month.

characters.name: March Hare
characters.physical_description: A hare with long ears like chimneys, sitting upright at a tea-table. He has a nervous hurried manner and holds a teacup and watch.

characters.name: Dormouse
characters.physical_description: A tiny sleepy dormouse with round body and whiskers, fast asleep between the Hatter and March Hare. He is used as a cushion and is small enough to fit into a teapot.

characters.name: Two
characters.physical_description: An oblong flat playing-card man with hands and feet at the corners, patterned like a club. He is one of the gardeners, kneeling and painting roses.

characters.name: Five
characters.physical_description: An oblong flat playing-card man with hands and feet at the corners, patterned like a club. He is one of the gardeners holding a paint brush and painting roses red.

characters.name: Seven
characters.physical_description: An oblong flat playing-card man with hands and feet at the corners, patterned like a club. He is one of the gardeners painting roses and throwing himself flat on his face.

characters.name: Queen of Hearts
characters.physical_description: A stern playing-card queen with a crimson face when angry and a shrill loud voice. She wears a crown and royal gown and carries no weapon but shouts orders.

characters.name: King of Hearts
characters.physical_description: A playing-card king wearing a crown over a great judge's wig. He is timid-looking with spectacles and a note-book, dressed in royal robes.

characters.name: Knave of Hearts
characters.physical_description: A playing-card knave made entirely of cardboard with a flat printed face. He wears a court livery and carries the King's crown on a crimson velvet cushion.

characters.name: Bill
characters.physical_description: A small poor little lizard with a scaly tail and squeaking voice. He wears no clothes and is small enough to go down a chimney and be held up by guinea-pigs.

characters.name: Pat
characters.physical_description: A small Irish workman creature with a brogue, wearing laborer's clothes. He is seen digging and holding ladders and ropes outside a little house.

characters.name: Gryphon
characters.physical_description: A mythical gryphon with the head, wings and talons of an eagle and the body of a lion. He lies fast asleep in the sun with large paws and sharp eyes when awake.

characters.name: Mock Turtle
characters.physical_description: A sad calf-like turtle with large eyes full of tears and flappers. He sits lonely on a ledge of rock, sobbing heavily with a deep hollow voice.

characters.name: Executioner
characters.physical_description: A hooded executioner in dark court attire carrying an axe. He stands among the King, Queen and crowd disputing about beheading.

chapters.title: Down the Rabbit-Hole
chapters.summary: Bored on a hot riverbank, Alice follows a waistcoated White Rabbit down a rabbit-hole and falls slowly through a well of cupboards and shelves. She lands in a lamp-lit hall with locked doors, where a tiny golden key opens a fifteen-inch door onto a lovely garden she cannot enter. After drinking from a DRINK ME bottle she shrinks to ten inches but leaves the key out of reach, then weeps and tries an EAT ME cake to change her size again.
chapters.cover_description: A tiny ten-inch-high Alice looking up at a little glass table holding a tiny golden key, beside a fifteen-inch door opening onto a bright flower-filled garden, with a White Rabbit in a waistcoat hurrying away down a lamp-lit hall.

chapters.title: The Pool of Tears
chapters.summary: Grown to nine feet high, Alice cannot fit through the little garden door and weeps a large pool of tears. The White Rabbit flees at her voice, dropping his fan and gloves, and fanning herself makes Alice shrink, doubt her identity, and then slip splash into her own salt pool. There she meets a swimming Mouse, offends it with talk of cats and Dinah and dogs, then soothes it and leads a crowded party of fallen birds and animals to shore to hear its history.
chapters.cover_description: A giant nine-foot Alice sitting cramped in an underground hall, tears streaming into a vast salt pool around her, reaching for a tiny garden door, later shrunk small and swimming in her own tears.

chapters.title: A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale
chapters.summary: Soaked from the pool, Alice joins the birds and Mouse on the bank trying to get dry, first with the Mouse's dry history lecture and then with the Dodo's chaotic Caucus-race where everyone wins comfits and Alice gets a thimble. Alice then misunderstands the Mouse's long sad tale as a tail-shape about Fury, offending it until it leaves. She innocently praises her cat Dinah's hunting, frightening the whole party away and leaving her alone crying.
chapters.cover_description: Alice standing in a ring of dripping wet birds and animals on a muddy riverbank as the solemn Dodo presents her with a thimble, with the Mouse in the middle and the chaotic Caucus-race circle behind them.

chapters.title: The Rabbit Sends in a Little Bill
chapters.summary: Mistaken by the White Rabbit for his housemaid Mary Ann, Alice fetches his fan and gloves but drinks from a little bottle that makes her grow gigantic and trapped inside his house. Besieged by the Rabbit, Pat and Bill, she kicks Bill up the chimney, threatens them with Dinah, then shrinks by eating pebbles turned to cakes and escapes into the wood, where she plays with an enormous puppy before meeting a blue caterpillar on a mushroom.
chapters.cover_description: A giant girl wedged tight inside a tiny neat cottage, one huge arm sticking out of the window and one foot up the chimney, head pressed against the ceiling, while a small anxious White Rabbit in a waistcoat stares up from below.

chapters.title: Advice from a Caterpillar
chapters.summary: Alice is interrogated by the silent, hookah-smoking Caterpillar about who she is and proves her confusion by reciting a garbled poem. The Caterpillar crawls away leaving the clue that opposite sides of the mushroom change her size. After violent shrinking and growing into a serpent-like neck that provokes a Pigeon's attack, Alice carefully nibbles herself back to normal and then down to nine inches to approach a little house by the garden.
chapters.cover_description: A large blue caterpillar with folded arms smoking a long hookah sits atop a giant round mushroom, staring down at a small Victorian girl with long fair hair standing below in a sunlit woodland clearing.

chapters.title: Pig and Pepper
chapters.summary: Alice watches the Fish-Footman deliver the Queen's croquet invitation to the Frog-Footman, then pushes past nonsense at the door into a pepper-choked kitchen where the Duchess nurses a howling baby and the cook hurls dishes. The Duchess flings the baby to Alice to go play croquet, and outside Alice watches it turn into a pig that trots into the wood. In the wood the Cheshire Cat directs her to the mad Hatter and March Hare, then vanishes slowly leaving only its grin as Alice heads for the March
chapters.cover_description: A smoke-filled Victorian kitchen choked with pepper, with an ugly Duchess nursing a howling baby on a three-legged stool, a cook stirring a huge cauldron of soup, and a large grinning Cheshire Cat sitting on the hearth.

chapters.title: A Mad Tea-Party
chapters.summary: Alice joins the Mad Hatter, March Hare, and sleeping Dormouse for a rude, nonsensical tea-party where riddles have no answers, watches tell the day but not the hour, and Time is a quarrelsome person who has frozen them at eternal six o'clock. After the Dormouse's confusing tale of treacle-well sisters and endless place-changing, insulted Alice storms off, finds a door in a tree, and finally shrinks herself to enter the beautiful garden.
chapters.cover_description: Alice sitting at a long crowded tea-table set out under a large tree, with the Mad Hatter in his big hat and the March Hare on either side using a tiny sleeping Dormouse as a cushion among cluttered teacups, teapots, bread-and-butter and a milk-jug in endless six o'clock tea-time.

chapters.title: The Queen’s Croquet-Ground
chapters.summary: Alice finds three card-gardeners painting white roses red to avoid beheading by the Queen of Hearts, then stands up to the Queen when the royal procession arrives and hides the gardeners in a flower-pot. Forced to join a chaotic croquet game played with live flamingos, hedgehogs, and soldiers as arches, Alice confides in the appearing Cheshire Cat, whose beheading is then impossibly debated until the Cat vanishes and the Duchess is summoned.
chapters.cover_description: Alice in a Victorian dress struggling to hold a live pink flamingo as a croquet mallet on a ridged croquet ground, aiming at a live hedgehog ball through an arch made of a doubled-up soldier, with the furious Queen of Hearts shouting nearby.

chapters.title: The Mock Turtle’s Story
chapters.summary: Walking with the strangely pleasant Duchess, Alice endures a barrage of nonsense morals until the Queen threatens the Duchess away and resumes her execution-filled croquet game. The Queen then hands Alice to the Gryphon, who reveals no executions really happen and leads her to the weeping Mock Turtle to hear his history of sea-school lessons that lessen.
chapters.cover_description: Alice sits with the sleepy Gryphon before the sorrowful Mock Turtle weeping on a lonely ledge of rock by the sea, the iconic heart of the chapter's seaside school story.

chapters.title: The Lobster Quadrille
chapters.summary: The Mock Turtle and Gryphon describe and demonstrate the Lobster Quadrille for Alice, including the whiting's song and nonsense explanations about whitings, soles, and porpoises. Alice recounts her adventures and is made to recite two garbled lessons about the Lobster and the Owl and Panther. The Mock Turtle begins singing Beautiful Soup, but the cry that the trial is beginning sends the Gryphon hurrying Alice away.
chapters.cover_description: The Mock Turtle and the Gryphon solemnly dancing round and round Alice on the lonely seashore while the Mock Turtle sings sadly, illustrating the Lobster Quadrille with the sea behind them.

chapters.title: Who Stole the Tarts?
chapters.summary: The trial of the chained Knave of Hearts for stealing the Queen's tarts begins before the King as judge, with the White Rabbit reading the accusation and a scribbling jury led by Bill the Lizard. The Hatter is called first and gives nervous, nonsensical evidence about tea dates and twinkling while Alice begins growing larger and quarrels with the Dormouse. After the Hatter is dismissed shoeless under threat of beheading and the pepper-carrying cook refuses to testify and vanishes, Alice is shock
chapters.cover_description: Alice standing in a crowded absurd courtroom with the King and Queen of Hearts enthroned in crown and robes, the chained Knave of Hearts guarded by soldiers, the White Rabbit blowing a trumpet and reading a parchment scroll, and a large dish of tarts on a table in the center.

chapters.title: Alice’s Evidence
chapters.summary: Alice's trial of the Knave collapses into farce as she outgrows the court, overturns the jury-box, and exposes the King's invented rules and meaningless verses as proof of nothing. When the Queen demands sentence first, Alice rebels and calls them only a pack of cards, shattering the dream. She wakes on the bank in her sister's lap, runs off to tea, while her sister daydreams of Wonderland and Alice's future storytelling.
chapters.cover_description: Giant Alice standing defiant in a courtroom as the entire pack of playing-card courtiers flies up into the air and rains down upon her, the Queen shouting and the King cowering behind his book.
